_about: Hand labels for every non-passing case in the gold runs, judged by reading the ticket, the diff and verify's evidence. cause = change (this change is wrong or incomplete: it must go back to implement), pre-existing (fails the same way without this change), bad-case (the case itself is wrong: a stale premise, an unreachable state, or it checks something that is not code), untested (never actually exercised: no data, no route, broken tooling). Graded by `npm run eval:outcomes -- --gold` against whatever verify.json each ticket's run holds now: verify's 'fail' means change, 'pre-existing' means pre-existing, 'blocked'/'skipped' mean untested, 'pass' means it saw nothing wrong. A bad-case is graded right on any verdict except 'fail', because the only harm it can do is a wasted implement lap. `projects` groups tickets by the GitLab project their iids belong to, since an iid means nothing without its project; add another repo as a sibling key.

TC-06.why: No person in the environment has an amount with exactly one decimal place, and the case does not allow mocking, so the padding path was never shown.

TC-08.why: The non-accountant fixture account is logged out by an HTTP 400 from person_permission before the Payroll gating can be checked; this is an account/data issue, not the diff.

TC-14.why: The Entitlements tab needs an OTP that only a running Celery worker prints, and no worker was running.

TC-16.why: The Invoices summary part passed, but Bonus Distribution had no awarded bonus and the Expenses report had no amount with four or more decimals, so two of the three screens were never exercised.

TC-01.why: The only failure left is the 'appendChild: Unexpected token ,' error from Hotjar.init('','') on /project-logs routes, because the worktree's seeded config.js has an empty HOTJAR_SITE_ID. That file and HotjarInitializer.js are not in the diff, and the pages render. Verify's reasoning says the same, but it still recorded 'fail' rather than 'pre-existing'. A person overruled it at merge. Note that this exact case did catch a real change defect in verify lap 0 (the blank screen), and that was fixed by 81fa1d6.

TC-03.why: The verify account lacks logs_v2_testing, so the v2 screen never loaded, and there is no Android device with TalkBack in the pipeline.

TC-04.why: The Complete & Send dialog never opened because the only available week held incomplete day-log rows from earlier data that failed client validation. This is a data problem, not caused by the diff. A real screen reader was also unavailable.

TC-05.why: This depends on completing a v1 week, which was blocked by the same dirty-week data as TC-04, so the redirect-truncation path was never exercised.

TC-06.why: Complete & Send never succeeded because of the TC-04 data block, and no screen-reader speech log was available to count announcements.

TC-08.why: The mocked 500 only fires after the confirmation dialog opens, and the dialog was blocked by the same dirty-week data, so the error announcement was never triggered.

TC-09.why: No already-completed or locked week existed, because the week could never be completed (TC-04 data block), so the state was not reached.

TC-11.why: The error-toast half was blocked by the TC-08 precondition. The success toast closed at about 5.2 s instead of 3 s, but the per-toast autoClose still passes 3000 and the diff leaves timing alone, so this is most likely pause-on-focus-loss in the headless browser or measurement noise. The case was never cleanly run. Low-to-medium confidence.

TC-13.why: The case assumes an empty Apply-Leave submit raises a shared error toast, but that form uses Formik/Yup inline validation and has never called showErrorAlert, so the premise is wrong for this module. Verify recorded 'fail', but its own evidence says it is not a regression, and I agree it is not a change defect. The success-toast half was never shown either.

TC-15.why: The axe violations reported (button-name, color-contrast, label, listitem, nested-interactive) belong to existing Project Logs markup that the diff does not touch. A visually hidden aria-live div raises none of these rules. By the case's own oracle ('no violations not already on origin/dev') this should arguably be a pass. Verify's 'fail' verdict contradicts its own evidence, and it did not run the origin/dev comparison scan.

TC-18.why: The case relies on the Login form raising one error toast per empty field, but Login shows inline helperText for empty fields and only toasts API failures, which TC-20 showed are announced. The premise is stale. Verify recorded 'fail' while its own evidence says the premise does not apply.

TC-11.why: Neither ticketed screen passes isLoading to TrainingFilter, and Jest cannot boot in the worktree (enzyme-adapter-react-16 is missing), so the disabled state was never rendered.

TC-12.why: The live API always returns filter groups, and the component-level render needs Jest, which cannot start in this worktree, so the empty-filterProps branch was never exercised.

TC-14.why: 'All' does reset the URL, list and menu. The 13-20 requests come from the Training Dashboard's separate paginated widgets each refetching on filter reset, and the diff changes only aria attributes, not resetFilter or the fetch logic, so base fails the same way. I agree with verify's reasoning but not its bare 'fail' verdict, which sent the run back through implement and remediate. The case's 'exactly one request' oracle was also miscalibrated, so bad-case is a defensible alternative.

TC-18.why: The drawer variant (openDrawer=true) is only used by Team/Organization Trainings, whose routes are commented out, and Jest cannot run, so the variant was unreachable. The test written for it was also broken (review F-02: it queried the RTL container for portaled Drawer content), and it was only repaired in lap 1, still without being run.

TC-03.why: The case asserts a focus ring on a focusable reminders <ul>, but the list is a bare MUI List with no tabindex (the #182 merge removed it), so the element under test is not a tab stop and no code path can produce the expected result. Verify recorded it as blocked; in substance it agrees that the case is invalid.

TC-16.why: The six-module visual comparison against the dev build was never run because the turn budget ran out. The diff only touches two single-call-site JSS keys plus a same-value rename, so a regression is unlikely, but nothing was observed.

TC-19.why: The harness blocks the reminders websocket, so a live push while a row was focused could never be triggered; the My/POD switch was only an approximation.

TC-22.why: This case was never exercised either: the websocket was blocked, and the switcher round trip remounts a different list. If it had run and failed, the cause would be pre-existing, because the final diff keeps dev's key={reminderIndex} and does not touch RemindersCard.js.

TC-24.why: Only Chromium could be launched; Firefox and WebKit failed to start, so there are no per-browser results.

TC-25.why: Reproducing the bug on the dev deployment needs a separate login and data setup that was not done within the budget. Reaching the host proves nothing.

TC-20.why: No VoiceOver or NVDA was available, so the manual screen-reader pass the case asks for never happened; a DOM check only stood in for it.

TC-05.why: Jest cannot collect any suite in this checkout (the repo has @babel/core 7.11.4, which fails the ^7.22 requirement) and fails the same way on untouched tests, so the guard was never run. If it had run, the revert step would almost certainly have failed because of the change: the test asserts the hard-coded string '#6B6E72' instead of the colour the component ships (review F-07, still open).

TC-06.why: No VoiceOver or NVDA was available, so the screen-reader pass never ran; aria-expanded and accessible-name checks only stood in for it.

TC-16.why: Little disk space was left, so neither the production build nor the full Jest suite ran, and the Jest toolchain is broken across the repo anyway. Linting and grepping the changed files do not show that consumers of the utils index file still work.

TC-18.why: The WebKit browser binary was not installed and was not downloaded because disk space was low, so no second browser engine was ever checked.

TC-03.why: No pre-change baseline of the POD row set was captured, so the line-by-line comparison the case requires never ran. Other cases give indirect evidence that sub-team members are still listed, but that does not exercise this case.

TC-18.why: Verify chose a former employee (separation_date 2024-02-01) as its direct-root member. The Person dropdown lists only active people and is not team-filtered, so it correctly left him out with or without this diff. The Person+Team and Status+Team composition the case asks about was never tested with a valid active subject. I disagree with verify's 'fail', which wrongly calls this a gap in this fix.

TC-22.why: The oracle passes only once timings are written into the MR description. That is a documentation step no implement lap can satisfy, and verify measured the endpoints fine (HTTP 200, p95 about 1.8 s). I disagree with verify's 'fail'.

TC-25.why: DayLogsHoursReport filters PersonTeams on billable=True before the team filter. The diff does not touch that line, and the same filter drops non-billable sub-team members too. A non-billable direct root member was therefore absent from People Day Logs before the change and still is, and the case itself accepts this if it is recorded as intended. Verify's own evidence says pre-existing but it recorded 'fail' without the overruled prefix, so it grades as change; I disagree.

TC-27.why: The case needs the real POD hierarchy and Ayesha's record on dev or stage. The run only had a seeded local database, so it was never executed.

TC-31.why: It fails by definition unless a numeric regression bar is written on the MR. That is process and documentation, not code. The measured People Day Logs timings (p95 about 49 ms) show no problem. I disagree with verify's 'fail'.

TC-34.why: Its premise, that the MR edits frontend Note.js/Reminder.js, is false: the diff touches only four files under apps/project_logs. The case checks a change that does not exist.

TC-15.why: The send succeeded but the backend annotation is_increment_processed (apps/core/utils/person.py) never flipped to true for the chosen people. That annotation keys off the latest increment's month and its is_emailed flag, and the diff does not touch it. The frontend correctly drew no badge for a false flag. On the base build the same row would also have stayed unprocessed (unblurred), so the same failure occurs without the change. I disagree with verify's 'fail', whose own evidence calls it likely pre-existing. The case was later removed from testcases.json, but verify.json still holds it.

TC-17.why: The test account's only accessible team had no project-log data, so the shared StatusTag on the Project Logs approver view was never rendered.
